Incident Bot: [PAGER] Networking - Azure UK West - DNS resolution anomalies detected for private connectivity to on-prem clusters. Severity: P2. Alerts: dns-resolve-failures-ukwest. Auto-page sent to oncall.  
Alice (oncall): acked. I'm on it. details? 
Incident Bot: Alerts show spike starting 11:02 UTC, increased NXDOMAIN and timeouts from our VPC endpoints used by Private deployments. Affected hostnames: private.redwood-inference.ukwest.* and customer CPE resolvers behind private link. Autoretries failing. 
Alice (oncall): ok running quick checks. ping to private resolver from ukwest-bastion... 
Ben (network): I'm joining. looks like the region's DNS fabric is intermittently returning SERVFAIL and TTL values are oscillating. Could be a zone transfer storm or upstream authoritative glitch. 
Carla (SRE): symptoms seen in logs: downstream on-prem agents report DNS lookup latencies 2-15s, causing model inference RPC timeouts around 30s. A handful of customers on Dedicated/Private have reported errors. 
Eve (SE): customer C: "we're seeing 504s and disconnected sessions" — working with them now. impact: some batch jobs failing, interactive latency high. 
Tom (Customer Success): Notifying account teams for customers with UK-West Private endpoints. Will post updates. 
Ben (network): running nslookup from ukwest-gw1 ->

```
$ nslookup private.redwood-inference.ukwest.svc.cluster.local 10.1.2.53
Server: 10.1.2.53
Address: 10.1.2.53#53
*** server can't find private.redwood-inference.ukwest.svc.cluster.local: SERVFAIL
```

But from a different AZ resolver it returns with high TTLs: 

```
$ nslookup private.redwood-inference.ukwest.svc.cluster.local 10.1.4.53
Server: 10.1.4.53
Address: 10.1.4.53#53
Name: private.redwood-inference.ukwest.svc.cluster.local
Address: 10.10.5.12
TTL: 18
```

Ben (network): TTLs flipping between 0-300 across resolvers -> suggests authoritative cluster in region is flapping or we're seeing inconsistent cache state across AZs. Could also be an Azure DNS forwarding chain bug. 
Alice (oncall): immediate mitigation idea: pin Private endpoints to secondary resolver pool (ukwest-secondary) for affected customers to avoid the flaky AZ. Also add short-term TTL override in our edge cache to prevent repeated lookups. Will coordinate rollback plan. 
Dinesh (Platform Eng): I can push a routing rule to our control plane to prefer ukwest-secondary for private DNS queries for affected projects. Will stage canary for one tenant then scale. 
Carla (SRE): Can we also add a fallback to public resolution for non-sensitive names while retaining private path for sensitive ones? That could reduce timeouts for non-critical control plane calls. 
Ben (network): caution: forwarding to public resolvers could expose internal names if misconfigured. need explicit allowlist. 
Alice (oncall): taking the page to implement: 1) add per-tenant resolver override to ukwest-secondary for currently impacted Dedicated/Private customers, 2) apply short-lived edge TTL=8s for private hostnames to smooth caches, 3) run continuous nslookup probes to track variance. Rolling out now for tenant 'acme-corp' canary. 
Incident Bot: deploybot: rollout started: resolver-override-v2 -> canary -> acme-corp (job 984712). 
Eve (SE): acme-corp confirms improvement within 2 minutes: "resolves are back to normal, inference latency dropping" :thumbsup: 
Tom (Customer Success): informing three customers in UK West private cohort about workaround and ETA for fix. customers asked for timeline on permanent fix. 
Ben (network): raising with Azure support / escalation - I have case 123456789 opened. Asking Azure to check regional DNS authoritative cluster and forwarding plane. 
Carla (SRE): metrics: service timeouts down from 14%->3% for canary tenant after override. Rolling to next 4 tenants. 
Alice (oncall): rolling to all impacted tenants now. ETA 22 minutes. Will monitor error budgets and latency percentiles. 
Incident Bot: monitor: dns-pulse-synth reports variance down but still occasional SERVFAIL from resolver 10.1.2.53. 
Ben (network): Azure replied: they're seeing elevated control-plane restarts in a subset of DNS nodes in UK West, investigating. Suggested temporary customer-side routing to alternative resolvers. 
Dinesh (Platform Eng): logging config pushed to limit retry storms on clients (increase backoff), and added circuit breaker to prevent cascading RPCs when DNS fails. 
Carla (SRE): customer impact summary for post-incident review: - Affected: ~7 Dedicated/Private tenants in UK-West. - Window: 11:02-12:05 UTC (partial mitigation from 11:12 with canary overrides) - Symptoms: DNS SERVFAIL/long TTLs -> client request timeouts, job failures, transient 502/504s. - Mitigation: resolver override to ukwest-secondary, increased client backoff, short TTL edge caching. - Root cause: under investigation by Azure (control-plane node restarts / forwarding inconsistency). 
Eve (SE): customers have accepted the workaround and asked for a followup summary and whether logs were exposed. We confirmed no sensitive hostnames were forwarded to public resolvers. 
Tom (Customer Success): sending proactive incident email with timeline and mitigation steps. 
Alice (oncall): marking incident as monitoring. will keep channel open until Azure confirms full regional stabilization and our metrics have been stable for 30m. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup: 
Ben (network): followup action: create runbook addition for resolver-override procedure and coordinate with product to add UI for emergency resolver preference. 
Carla (SRE): filing postmortem stub and will add detailed logs + correlation graphs. 
Incident Bot: [RESOLVE] alerts de-escalated to watch after 12:10 UTC, but channel open for updates. 
Alice (oncall): last check: synth errors at 0.8%, token latency back to baseline. closing to monitoring, will update postmortem when ready. 
Tom (Customer Success): customers notified, closing loop once PM summary posted. 
Alice (oncall): final note: if anyone gets direct Azure update, drop it here and we'll attach to postmortem. Good job team.
